RCV:
This was a roll-call vote. Each MEP's position is recorded by name and published, which is what this site is built on: you can see how every MEP, every national party and every political group voted.

A roll-call is held when a political group, or at least 40 MEPs, request one before the vote. That is why the list of roll-calls is not the whole Parliament: it is the subset of votes that were contested enough for someone to want the votes on the record.

Roll-calls are typically a bit less than half of all the votes of a sitting, and they carry almost all of the political weight: final votes on legislation, the amendments that matter, and the votes people ask about afterwards.
HAND:
This vote was taken by show of hands. The European Parliament records only the overall result (adopted, rejected, lapsed) and does not record which MEP raised a hand, so there is nothing to look up for a single MEP.

Show-of-hands votes are used for the less contested items — procedural questions, amendments nobody asks for a recorded vote on, and whole reports where the outcome is already clear. That is why they are numerous: most votes of a sitting week are decided this way.

If you need the individual positions, only a roll-call vote would give them. Any political group (or at least 40 MEPs) can ask for one before the vote, and they do so precisely for the votes they consider politically significant — which is why the votes on this site are a biased, but relevant, sample of what the Parliament voted.
ELECTRONIC:
This vote was taken with the electronic voting system, but without a roll-call. The Parliament publishes the totals — how many MEPs voted for, against or abstained — and not the identity of each voter.

The Member States' representatives vote this way on amendments and reports where a recorded vote was not requested. Only when a group or 40 MEPs ask for a roll-call does the Parliament publish the per-MEP list, and only then does an MEP's individual vote become public.

So the totals are exact, but they cannot be attributed to a country, a political group or a person.
SECRET:
This vote was a secret ballot. The Parliament counts the votes and publishes the totals, but the ballot is by definition anonymous: no record links a vote to an MEP, and none is kept.

Secret ballots are used for appointments — the President and Vice-Presidents of the Parliament, the Ombudsman, and similar personal decisions — where the rules of procedure require members to be able to vote without pressure.

The totals remain meaningful, the individual positions simply do not exist.
default:
This vote was not a roll-call vote. The European Parliament published the overall result, but not the individual positions of the MEPs, so there is nothing to attribute to a country, a group or a person.

Only roll-call votes produce a per-MEP record. For everything else — show of hands, electronic votes without a roll-call, secret ballots — the published data stops at the totals, and for show of hands even the totals are not always counted.

Groups request a roll-call for the votes they consider politically significant, so the MEP-level data on this site covers those votes only.
